summary: This work presents a fault-tolerant framework for preparing arbitrary logical states in the four-legged cat code using error-detectable operations in 3D superconducting cavities coupled to ancilla qubits. Numerical simulations achieve logical infidelities of $10^{-4}$ with quadratic suppression of first-order errors in photon loss and dephasing channels.
motivation: Efficient high-fidelity logical state preparation is essential for magic state distillation and quantum error correction, yet existing approaches struggle to balance control complexity against resource overhead while suppressing dominant incoherent errors.
method: The protocol engineers error-detectable coherent state discrimination $\mathcal{M}_{|\beta\rangle}$ through displacement, photon-number-selective ancilla flips, and reverse displacement, combined with parity measurement and existing error-detectable $Z_c(\theta)$ and $ZZ_c(\theta)$ rotations to realize a universal gate set $\{\mathcal{M}_P, Z_c(\theta), ZZ_c(\theta), \mathcal{M}_X, H_c\}$ on realistic 3D cavity-QED hardware.
result: Two-qubit entangled state preparation achieves logical infidelity $(2.74 \pm 1.09) \times 10^{-4}$ at $\alpha = 2.9$ with $>95\%$ success probability; scaling analysis confirms $\bar{f}_L \propto s^{2.12 \pm 0.09}$, demonstrating first-order error suppression and robustness across a continuous family of target states.
